Close reading requires a supported open book, eyes aimed at a source line, an annotation referring to that same line and separate page/tool hand roles. Its complete effects include text, which is closed in this frozen core; there is no independently required source line or annotation. A generic book or workbench cannot substitute.

The extra facial demonstration competes with the task and equipment route; A1 gives the subject a more direct working presence. Profile gates remain unselected.

Supportive forearm hand needs health-access/rehabilitation context and a consent-led stabilizing relation. Neither context nor a second supportive actor is established; a metal cuff is not a consenting helper hand. Do not infer treatment or consent from the frame.

It is a compatible pause, but adds a head-support mechanism and distracts from the one external path; A1 is preferred.

Traceable nominated-hand/object grip or support is already fully realized by the independent B0 palm edge, thumb and handle-to-clamp clause and is retained in A1. It introduces no new cue; record genuine redundancy rather than falsely attributing independent baseline geometry to this source.

This frozen scope does not establish that adult premise. A hand resting at the bench is not the source whole torso-load configuration; no support fragment is borrowed.
